search_strategy: The agent never used a Mattermost REST search endpoint; instead it dumped every channel's full post history to /tmp/rec/chat/<channel>.txt (via a Python script hitting the Mattermost API, ~10k messages across 12 channels) and every wiki page (body+comments) to /tmp/rec/txt/ and /tmp/rec/wiki/, plus every mail message to /tmp/rec/mail/. It hit two self-inflicted bugs early (a python write-then-read-same-file truncation bug that zeroed the chat/mail dumps, and a literal-backslash-n bug that put whole channels on one line) and recovered from both by rewriting the fetch scripts, at some real cost in steps (~1620-1940). Gitea issues (all ~750, tokenized) and BookStack pages (228, with 21 lost to a 429 rate limit initially, re-fetched) were dumped and grepped for 'run identity/run_hash/RunIdentity/fingerprint' etc. From step ~1988 onward, the dominant strategy was iterative grep-then-read: grep the local chat dump for a keyword (run_identity, component, response_format, system_prompt, run_id, 'v3', RunIdentityError), then read the surrounding 20-60 lines of the matched channel.txt file to get the full multi-turn exchange (rather than trusting the single matched line). This is why so many facts were recovered even though 15 of 48 individual remarks never appear verbatim in the visible transcript: reading wide windows around a grep hit repeatedly swept up several neighbouring remarks in the same region (e.g. reading code-review.txt 2320-2360 for one grep hit surfaced both the h1 herring and its rev1 reversal). Wiki and mail were dumped and grepped but yielded almost nothing task-specific (4 pages mention 'identity' generically; no page discusses run_identity/RUN_IDENTITY/fingerprint for this ticket) -- essentially the entire hidden-requirements recovery came from chat, consistent with the ticket's own 'this task has no wiki or mail carriers' framing for the world arm. The agent kept an explicit running list of the 12 component keys and revised its belief about the nocache path's uuid4 usage mid-investigation when it hit a conflicting Mar-31 message, then went and read the fuller context before finalizing (steps 34-38, notably 'Analysis: Critical nocache design ... But a Mar 31 message says uuid4. Need to read that context.', line 2535). It wrote a full unit test file (12, then 19, then 26 passing tests) exercising exactly the observability table before pushing, and re-read its own diff once more before committing, catching and fixing one remaining gap itself (run_id not yet keyword-only on __call__) by re-citing a specific remark it had read.
end_reason: Not applicable -- run scored reward 1 with all 8 hidden-requirement facts, the suite, and provenance (pushed/CI green/deployed) all passing. PR 737 merged to main as 3a83f74, CI status 'success', deploy requested by the CI job.
notable: line 2535: the agent explicitly caught its own tentative belief (uuid4 minted inside compute_run_identity) contradicting a later message and paused to re-read context before finalizing -- textbook herring-then-reversal handling.

lines 10310-10328: after committing, the agent re-reviewed the record once more, found it had left run_id as a plain (non-keyword-only) kwarg on __call__, explicitly cited the g4.r2.l4 remark ('named keyword only arg on __call__ not something we dig out of **kwargs'), and amended the commit to fix it -- direct evidence a specific clue drove a specific code change.

15 of 48 remarks (31%) never appear as literal text anywhere in the visible transcript (verified by direct grep for each remark's distinctive phrasing across the full 10732-line transcript) -- yet every one of the 8 graded facts still scored 1, because clues.spread() plants 2-6 redundant carriers per fact and the agent's grep-then-read-wide-window strategy swept up at least one carrier of every fact.

The redundancy pattern is uneven: g4.r1.rule and g4.r2.failure_behavior each had 5-6 carrying remarks and the agent found most of them; g4.r1.scope and g4.r1.exclusions_or_crossover had thinner margins (2-3 carriers each) but the agent happened to find the single most information-dense remark in each group (l-backend-default for scope; rev1 for exclusions_or_crossover), which alone states almost the entire fact.

The implementation's inline comments closely paraphrase specific remarks it read (e.g. the LLM.backend docstring restates l-backend-default's 'naming the default cant change identity' almost verbatim; the __call__ comment 'Refuse first, create afterwards' restates l12's 'check moved ahead of run dir creation'), which is strong evidence the agent was translating specific corpus text into code rather than pattern-matching from the ticket or the real curator API surface alone.
